headline: Highest risk is medium: PaddleOCR can ingest documents/images while Taipy can orchestrate data workflows, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and workflow-conflict risks without documented isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: PaddleOCR ingests documents/images and can call APIs, while Taipy is a data-engineering workflow tool. If Taipy consumes OCR output or shared files by default, attacker-controlled document text could be treated as instructions. No shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Taipy reads PaddleOCR output from a shared file or pipeline without provenance checks, injection is plausible.
IF OCR output is rendered into prompts or task definitions, attacker text can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to OCR outputs before Taipy consumes them.
Strip instruction-like text from OCR results before downstream use.
Require a human review step for any OCR-derived task text.
Isolate the handoff directory from editable user content.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for all OCR-to-workflow inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images and has allowlisted egress; Taipy shows no data classes touched and no egress. The pair lacks a documented shared workspace or shared principal, so leakage is possible only through an unshown integration path, which keeps blast radius limited and uncertainty low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace, OCR inputs may be exposed to Taipy workflows.
IF PaddleOCR sends extracted content through its allowlisted egress to a third party, document contents can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Use separate directories for OCR inputs and Taipy outputs.
Disable network egress for OCR jobs that handle sensitive documents.
Review allowlist destinations before processing confidential files.
Delete intermediate OCR artifacts after each run.
requires-engineering: enforce per-job access controls on shared storage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: PaddleOCR has allowlisted network egress and browser capability, while Taipy is a data-engineering/scheduler tool with no explicit write or network permissions shown. Overlap is not documented, so a direct write conflict is not provable; the main risk is only if an external orchestrator gives both write access to the same mutable resource.
conditions: IF an orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory or dataset, they can race on shared state.
IF Taipy schedules jobs that mutate files produced by PaddleOCR, stale overwrites become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same dataset.
Check timestamps before overwriting generated files.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR produces document-derived text, and Taipy is a workflow/scheduler platform that may act on upstream outputs. If Taipy treats OCR output as authoritative without verification, transcription errors can cascade into downstream actions or reports. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty warrants medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Taipy uses OCR output as an input dataset without validation, transcription errors propagate downstream.
IF downstream Taipy jobs trigger actions from extracted text, a single OCR mistake can affect multiple work products.
mitigations: Add a validation step before Taipy consumes OCR output.
Sample-check OCR results against source documents.
Flag low-confidence OCR fields for manual review.
Keep raw source documents alongside extracted text.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rejection logic.

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents/images and has allowlisted egress; Taipy shows no touched data classes or compliance claims. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a limited compliance gap is plausible if sensitive documents are routed through PaddleOCR's egress path. The other agent is not cited for a specific mismatch because none is stated.
conditions: IF sensitive documents include regulated personal data and PaddleOCR egresses them to a third party, a compliance review is required.
IF Taipy stores the same regulated data under a different retention policy, retention mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Confirm whether the documents contain regulated data before processing.
Keep regulated files off any network-enabled OCR path.
Document retention rules for OCR artifacts.
Purge temporary files after each run.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls across the pipeline.
